data.title: Nvidia's stock heads for a stretch of weekly losses unseen since 2008
data.description:
By Hannah Pedone

One fund manager says the continued uncertainty makes Nvidia 'vulnerable' to more selling, even as the company has erased $811 billion in market value in the past seven days

Nvidia's stock is down for the seventh week in a row, a stretch of consecutive losses not seen in nearly two decades.

A cascade of factors has left the stock reeling, most notably Jensen Huang's resignation and the Nvidia (NVDA) board's investigation into whether he compromised national security or revealed corporate secrets. But the stock had been under pressure even before that, with investors questioning the sustainability of artificial-intelligence demand.

Nvidia shares haven't fallen for seven weeks in a row since July 2008, when it had to issue a profit warning and was working to address defects in some of its chips.

Shares of Nvidia were trading 5% lower on Friday. They've lost 13.6% so far this week and they're down 41.2% from their peak close achieved in early October.

Nvidia's stock is down for seven days in a row, over which it has shed $811 billion in market cap. That's roughly the size of JPMorgan Chase, which has a $847 billion market cap, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

The stock's "weakness despite strong earnings shows how much it will take to restore confidence." David Miller, the chief investment officer at Catalyst Funds, told MarketWatch.

On Tuesday, Nvidia reported blockbuster earnings results and raised its revenue outlook for next year, but that wasn't enough to stem the bleeding.

Seaport Research analyst Jay Goldberg told MarketWatch that fund managers who previously held Nvidia because it was a "safety stock" are now "rotating out" amid the turmoil.

So what comes next?

Goldberg expects things to stabilize next week. "I don't think it keeps falling," he said, though admittedly "there is no one in a hurry to buy it until we know who the next CEO is."

But Miller thinks Nvidia's stock is "vulnerable" to more selling. The length of the losing streak alone "tells us very little about where the bottom is," he told MarketWatch.

"A sharp rebound is certainly possible, but I would want greater clarity on permanent leadership and the investigations, along with continued execution on customer demand and product deliveries, before becoming confident in a sustained recovery," he added.

-Hannah Pedone

data.title: Anthropic's stock slides closer to IPO price and drags down the AI trade
data.description:
By Emily Bary

Anthropic's inability to hold its opening stock price has been seen as 'bad for the rest of tech'

Anthropic finished with a $1.29 trillion valuation on Thursday.

There was no honeymoon period for Anthropic after its record-breaking initial public offering.

Shares of the AI company are down more than 9% in morning action on Friday, making for a gloomy second day of trading. Anthropic's stock (ANT) is at $88.16, well below its $111.50 opening price, and falling closer to its $83 IPO price.

It's a downbeat sign for the broader technology ecosystem as well, with AI stocks taking a beating across the board. Among notable losers are shares of Sandisk (SNDK), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Dell Technologies (DELL), Nebius Group (NBIS) and Arm Holdings (ARM).

"The vast majority of this continued selling pressure in the last 24 hours feels more to do with" the Anthropic IPO than it does with some less-than-perfect earnings reports in the technology sector, according to Jefferies trading-desk analyst Jeffrey Favuzza.

He wrote in a note to clients that Anthropic's inability to hold its opening price and the downward pressure in Friday's premarket action is being viewed as "bad for the rest of tech."

Anthropic's IPO was seen as a tentpole event for the AI trade. The company finished with a $1.29 trillion valuation on Thursday, according to Dow Jones Market Data. Friday's action brings that down to $1.16 trillion.

"Anthropic's strong debut alongside a falling technology sector suggests investors still believe in AI but are becoming more selective about what they will pay for that growth," David Miller, the chief investment officer at Catalyst Funds, said in emailed comments.

Some analysts initiated coverage of Anthropic's stock after Thursday's close, chiming in with mixed views.

"We are cautious, not negative," wrote Seaport Research's Jay Goldberg, who launched coverage of shares with a neutral rating.

He called Anthropic an "incredible company," but also one "asking for an incredible leap of faith by investors."

"We think the company will need time to grow into its valuation and answer some very big questions about its growth trajectory," he continued. For instance, the company saw 43% revenue growth from the second quarter to the third quarter. That compared with a much faster 144% growth rate from the first quarter to the second quarter.

Goldberg referred to that as a "worrying" deceleration. "To merit its valuation, it will need to see much higher growth rates over the next two years," he added.

William Blair's Arjun Bhatia was more upbeat, calling Anthropic a "generational company driving a generational technology shift" as he began his own coverage of the stock with an outperform rating.

"Questions about the future are worth asking, even those that don't have an answer at this point," he wrote.

But at the same time, he and his team "don't want to miss the forest for the trees."

"We think AI is a generational shift in the tech landscape, and Anthropic is leading the charge in developing AI with a select handful of other companies," Bhatia wrote. "Over the next decade, we think Anthropic is only going to become more important and consume a greater portion of enterprise spend," meaning it will command more of the budget that businesses have to allocate toward technology.

-Emily Bary

data.title: Merchants & Marine Bancorp, Inc. Announces Third Quarter Financial Results
data.description:
Merchants & Marine Bancorp, Inc. (), the parent company of TownBridge Bank, reported net income available to common shareholders through the third quarter of 2026 of $12.84 million, or $9.13 per share, compared with earnings of $2.30 million, or $1.73 per share, in the same period of the prior year. Gross income through the third quarter totaled $73.34 million, an increase of 82.02% from the prior year. Balance sheet footings increased by 36.95% to $1.30 billion during the 12 months ended September 30, 2026. Net loans grew to $692.90 million over the trailing 12 months from $466.73 million, an increase of 48.46%. Total deposits increased 58.65% during the same period, from $603.81 million at September 30, 2025, to $957.97 million. Significant growth in the balance sheet and in earnings is primarily the result of the successful acquisition of Farmers-Merchants Bank, Breaux Bridge, LA (FM Bank), which closed on April 1, 2026.

Selected financial highlights:

  • Net loans increased to $692.90 million at the end of the third quarter, up from $677.13 million at the end of the second quarter.

  • Total interest income during the third quarter increased to $16.99 million from $12.67 million during the same period in 2025, an increase of 34.11%. Net interest income for the quarter totaled $13.24 million, compared with $9.69 million in the third quarter of 2025.

  • Deposit costs totaled 74 basis points in the third quarter of 2026, essentially unchanged from 73 basis points in the second quarter of 2026.

  • The ratio of loans past due 30-89 days stood at 2.54% of total loans at the end of the third quarter of 2026, an increase from 1.70% at the end of the second quarter. The ratio of non-accrual loans totaled 1.87% of total loans at the end of the third quarter of 2026 compared to 1.94% at the end of the second quarter. The Allowance for Credit Losses (ACL) totaled $7.95 million, or 1.13% of total loans.

  • Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income (AOCI) mark-to-market losses in the securities portfolio totaled ($11.80 million) at the end of the third quarter of 2026, representing 3.05% of the $386.69 million securities portfolio. The increase in AOCI from ($5.81 million) during the second quarter is a result of increases in market rates during the quarter.

  • On-balance sheet liquidity levels remain healthy, with cash and cash equivalents totaling $94.42 million at the end of the third quarter of 2026. In addition to these large cash balances, the Company's investment portfolio remains highly liquid, with a significant portion of the portfolio able to be liquidated with minimal losses.

  • In addition to the sizable on-balance sheet liquidity position, the Company has more than $200 million in additional borrowing capacity at the Federal Home Loan Bank of Dallas and the Federal Reserve.

“We continued a strong earnings trend in the third quarter of 2026, with pre-tax, pre-provision earnings of approximately $2.26 million. This was inclusive of a $158 thousand loss on securities sales as we repositioned the portfolio to better fit the bank after our acquisition of Farmers-Merchants Bank earlier this year,” remarked Casey Hill, the company’s Chief Financial Officer. He continued: “Core earnings continue to accelerate as we realize certain efficiencies after our most recent merger. We do expect these efficiencies to further materialize as we undergo our core and systems conversion in January of 2027. Since the acquisition of FM Bank, we have been operating two core systems along with several other duplicative systems that, once fully merged, are expected to produce significant cost savings.”

“In addition,” continued Hill, “our teams across our Family of Brands continue to perform well. The increase in revenue from our legacy brands, paired with the continued high performance of the FM Bank team bodes well for continued lift in future earnings. While we are experiencing tailwinds in the form of slight elevations in past due loans, we feel confident that the bulk of these should be resolved prior to year-end and are not indicative of broader erosion in our loan portfolio. We are very optimistic about financial performance going forward.”

“Our third quarter results reflect the strong progress our teams are making in bringing FM Bank into our Family of Brands operating model,” remarked Clayton Legear, Chairman & Chief Executive Officer. “Our talented bankers have done an outstanding job of integrating a sizable new brand while continuing to operate our legacy brands at ever stronger levels. We remain encouraged that our operating model allows our brand bankers to serve their clients and communities with the same care and attention they always have and to drive strong results. We are on track for our core systems conversion in January 2027, and we are excited about the enhanced efficiencies and capabilities that will follow.”

Legear continued: “The third quarter also marked an important milestone for our Company. Effective September 28, 2026, our bank charter name officially changed from Merchants & Marine Bank to TownBridge Bank, providing a shared corporate identity for our growing Family of Brands. While our bank charter name has changed, our commitment to our Family of Brands operating model has not. Each of our brands will continue to retain their unique identity, and to be led by local bankers who know their clients, understand their communities, and make decisions close to home. Backed by our Battle-Ready Balance Sheet, our talented team of bankers in every Brand, and the strong momentum building across our Family of Brands, we are better positioned than ever for the future.”

Share Repurchase Program

The share repurchase program authorized by the Board of Directors in the second quarter, covering up to three percent (3%) of the Company's outstanding common stock, remains in effect through June 30, 2027.

Merchants & Marine Bancorp, Inc. () is the parent company of TownBridge Bank, a Mississippi chartered community bank serving the Gulf South region. Originally founded in 1899 as Merchants & Marine Bank and reborn during 1932, the Bank adopted the TownBridge Bank name in 2026 to provide a shared charter identity for its growing Family of Brands while allowing its community banking and financial services brands to retain the local identifies, leadership, and relationships that make them distinctive. The Bank offers banking services to customers in Southern Mississippi and Coastal Alabama under its legacy Merchants & Marine Bank brand, in Southeastern Louisiana through its Mississippi River Bank brand, and in the Acadiana Region of Louisiana through its Farmers-Merchants Bank brand. It offers mortgage financing through its Canvas Mortgage brand, cannabis banking through its CannaFirst Financial brand, and access to government-guaranteed credit through its Voyager Lending brand. It provides bank operational, risk, and support services through its Community of Resources bank services brand. For more information on Merchants & Marine Bancorp, Inc., visit https://townbridge.bank/investors/

data.title: Dollar falls as Fed-fueled rally stalls; lower US yields help yen
data.description:
Key points:
  • Dollar index still near strongest level since early April 2025
  • Falling Treasury yields support low-yielding currencies
  • Yen firms after Japanese core inflation hits 2.2%
  • Bitcoin at fresh four-month low

By Saqib Iqbal Ahmed

The dollar fell broadly on Friday as a weeks-long rally fueled by bets on a hawkish Federal Reserve lost momentum, but waning appetite for riskier currencies limited the losses.

The dollar index fell 0.2% to 103.75, just short of the 103.9 level it touched in the previous session, its highest since April 2025. The index was on track to snap an eight-session winning streak and is up 1.7% so far this month.

The dollar's rally accelerated on November 10, when hotter-than-expected US inflation data reinforced bets that the Fed would tighten policy and Fed Governor Christopher Waller said a 50-basis-point hike in December should be considered.

"I think the momentum has stalled for the dollar ... but I think it's a little bit early to pick a top for the dollar," said Marc Chandler, chief market strategist at Bannockburn Capital Markets.

US Treasury yields dropped on Friday as a multitude of AI-related concerns weighed on global stocks and Anthropic's record market debut on Thursday did little to revive investor confidence. On Friday, investors sought out safe-haven assets. Lower Treasury yields also boosted the relative appeal of the Swiss franc. The dollar slipped 0.5% against the franc.

"When US rates are falling, low-yielding currencies look better," Chandler said.

Still, strategists see the dollar continuing to draw some support from the outlook for a hawkish Fed.

Chris Turner, global head of markets at ING, said that while there is only a weak case for another steep correction in equities, "there is no reason for the Fed to drop its hawkish rhetoric anytime soon."

He pointed to the release next week of the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index, a key inflation gauge for the Fed, which Turner said will likely confirm that the US central bank needs to act.

"For FX, that means a continued strong dollar and continued pressure on popular carry trades," he said.

In FX carry trades, investors borrow in low-yielding currencies, such as the Japanese yen and Swiss franc, to fund purchases of higher-yielding assets elsewhere, often in emerging markets.

YEN FIRMS ON INFLATION DATA

Against the yen , the dollar slipped 0.5% to 158.85, still close to levels at which Japanese authorities intervened in July to shore up the drooping currency.

"The yen has jumped today, helped by lower US rates and firm Japanese October CPI," Chandler said.

Japan's annual core inflation accelerated to 2.2% in October, staying above the central bank's 2% target for a second straight month and pointing to broadening price pressures that strengthen the case for a near-term rate hike by the Bank of Japan.

Analysts at Capital Economics argue that the yen's recent weakness is unlikely to last. With long-term inflation expectations now around target, further increases in yields would be mostly in real terms, which, combined with their view that US yields will fall, should prove yen-positive, the analysts said.

Meanwhile, sterling rose 0.1%, but remained near a one-year low against the dollar at $1.31065.

In cryptocurrency markets, bitcoin slipped to a fresh four-month low as investors avoided riskier investments. Bitcoin was last trading roughly flat on the day at $61,442.

data.title: Boeing leaves open possibility of more layoffs amid stalled production plans
data.description:
By Dan Catchpole

When pressed by one of its largest unions, Boeing management declined to say on Thursday if the company plans on further layoffs after an upcoming round next month.

"We asked if December 9 was the only date for (layoff notices) and were told Boeing didn't know," Bryan Corliss, a spokesman for the Society of Engineering Employees in Aerospace, told Reuters.

In early November, Boeing announced plans to cut 5% of the company's commercial airplanes division's roughly 50,000 employees through attrition and layoffs. The cuts were needed because it is taking longer than expected for the company to increase output of its 737 MAX jet, its largest moneymaker, the division's CEO Stephanie Pope explained in a memo to employees at the time.

Asked about SPEEA's comment, a Boeing spokesperson told Reuters, “We continue to work through an established process to ensure our workforce can support our customer commitments. We are committed to treating everyone with dignity and respect and will communicate details with impacted employees once decisions are finalized.”

The company is trying to increase 737 production rate from 42 jets a month to 47, which it had planned to reach this past summer. Last month, Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg told investors that the company now expects to reach that target in early 2027.

On Thursday, SPEEA told its roughly 17,000 members that Boeing managers told union officials that:

"Employment at all Boeing Commercial Airplanes sites is under review, but layoffs won’t necessarily impact all sites.

"These will not be across-the-board layoffs, but rather targeted layoffs focused on which work statements are ending or can be ended.

"There will be no voluntary layoffs or buy-outs."

SPEEA members approved a new four-year contract with the company in early October. Boeing managers told the union that the cuts were not retaliation for the contract, which included a guaranteed 10% wage increase ​upon ratification, along with ⁠annual raises of 4% and the possibility of an additional 2% pay hike based on performance.

data.title: Bitcoin Hovers Near Four-Month Low as Traders Await U.S. PCE Data — Market Talk
data.description:
1035 ET - U.S. personal consumption expenditures inflation data for October will be a major catalyst for bitcoin and crypto prices, Nexo's Neil Steinhardt writes in a note. The data--the Federal Reserve's preferred gauge--will be released on Wednesday and can determine how firmly expectations for a rate increase at the Fed's December meeting are priced in, he says. In the meantime, Anthropic's performance after its stock market debut will drive AI sentiment while crypto exchange-traded fund flows remain the clearest gauge of institutional demand for bitcoin, Steinhardt adds. Bitcoin falls 0.2% to $61,400, having reached a four-and-a-half-month low of $61,225 earlier following a selloff in AI stocks, according to LSEG. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

1028 ET - Treasury yields are likely to trend lower as market volatility spurs demand for bonds, SanJac Alpha's Andrew Wells says. He is buying seven- to 10-year Treasurys as markets rotate out of risk assets. "We turned, I'd say in September, maybe early September, we began to turn more bullish on rates," Wells says. "So we began to turn constructive on the longer end of the curve...and have been doing that since." Wells expects Treasury buying to pick up further amid potential 1Q volatility around government debt ceiling debates. "We think there's definitely some room to go." (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)

1027 ET - The latest Canadian retail data confirms consumer spending will be a solid contributor to 3Q GDP but also signals slowing growth late in the quarter and into 4Q isn't entirely due to weakness in sectors exposed to U.S. tariffs, CIBC Capital Markets' Andrew Grantham says. Retail sales 0.8% in September and 1.2% in 3Q, with quarterly volumes up 1%. The advance estimate for October points to a 1.5% fall in sales. Grantham notes the Bank of Canada was already expecting below 1% growth in 4Q GDP, but says upcoming data for October GDP and November employment will still be important heading into the central bank's December rate decision to judge if there is downside risk to that already cautious forecast. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)

1017 ET - The run of weak Canadian data continues an early estimate retail sales dropped 1.5% on-month in October following a 0.8% advance the month before that was driven by higher prices. With September sales up a mere 0.1% in volume terms, Bank of Montreal's Benjamin Reitzes sees downside risk to the flash estimate monthly GDO contracted 0.1% in September. "The case for a follow up Bank of Canada rate hike in December is becoming increasingly challenging," the strategist says. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)

0957 ET - Sukuk or Islamic bond defaults remain rare globally, although uncertainty over recovering investments after a default persists, Fitch Ratings says. Only 0.17% of sukuk issued worldwide had defaulted as of the end of October, involving about $5 billion across roughly 160 instruments, according to the ratings agency. The default rate for U.S. dollar-denominated sukuk was 0.59%, compared with 0.93% for conventional dollar bonds in core sukuk markets. Fitch says no rated Gulf Cooperation Council sukuk has defaulted despite attacks in the region during the Iran conflict. However, differences in legal frameworks and limited precedents continue to complicate debt recovery. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)

0956 ET - A modest rise in core Canadian retail sales in September and an advance estimate for a sizeable decline in October sales supports Capital Economics' view the Bank of Canada has scope to wait until the New Year to lift interest rates again. That is especially the case with oil prices at their lowest in almost three months, economist Bradley Saunders says. He says the estimated 1.5% decline in October retail sales is disappointing, especially given that gasoline prices only fell 2% last month so aren't entirely responsible for the move. This chimes with the message from the continued weakness in consumer confidence, and the jump in the share of firms reporting insufficient demand as a barrier to production, Bradley adds.(robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)

0935 ET - The risk-off sentiment persists in Wall Street with the equity selloff and talks of steep interest rate increases by the Fed. But the fire sale may be creating buying opportunities. Newfleet's David Albrycht points to high yields touching 8.5%, bank loans near 10% and emerging market high yields at 8.4% as attractive options. He looks for high-quality bonds and opportunistic buying. "Haven't added yet but levels looking interesting," he says in an email. Meanwhile, Treasury yields are falling, with the 10-year at 4.984%. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)

0916 ET - Sterling has limited scope to extend recent gains against the euro, UBS Global Wealth Management analysts say in a note. "The pound has already strengthened on a trade-weighted basis, reducing valuation support." Euro positioning is heavily short, betting on a weaker currency, which leaves room for a reversal if France passes a budget later this month and political risk recedes, they say. UBS expects the euro to trade at 0.8400 pounds by March 2027 and 0.8500 in September 2027. The euro last trades flat at 0.8378 pounds, having reached a 19-month low of 0.8317 in late October, LSEG data show. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

0913 ET - Treasury yields and the dollar decline as investors rotate away from risky assets into the safety of bonds. The hype around Anthropic's blockbuster IPO fades as markets worry about AI's lofty ambitions. The decline in yields happens even as investors expect higher interest rates by the Fed to tame inflation. Brent crude is stable around $91. The WSJ Dollar Index falls 0.3%, with the greenback weakening 0.7% versus the yen. The 10-year yield slips below 5% to 4.972%. The two-year is at 4.675%, down from 4.777% yesterday. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)Andrew Kenningham works for Capital Economics. "France's Fiscal Arithmetic Remains Worrying — Market Talk," at 1440 GMT on Thursday, incorrectly said Kenningham works for Oxford Economics.

0907 ET - Credit spreads on euro corporate bonds widen as investors flee from risk assets towards safe-haven assets due to concerns about a possible slowdown in the artificial intelligence industry, LBBW's credit analysts say in a note. "Given the ongoing uncertainty, we do not expect a significant narrowing of spreads in the short term, but rather a sideways trend at the current elevated level." (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0855 ET - The euro should gradually recover against the dollar next year, UBS Global Wealth Management analysts say in a note. Euro short positioning--bets on the currency falling--looks stretched, they say. The potential passage of a French budget should help the euro, although a lasting recovery is more likely after the French presidential elections in the second quarter of 2027, they say. Lower oil prices should bring down inflation, meanwhile. "As the policy debate shifts from hikes toward a prolonged pause and eventually easing, the dollar should lose support." The euro rises 0.3% to $1.0994, having reached a 19-month low of $1.0952 on Wednesday, according to LSEG. UBS expects the euro to reach $1.16 by September 2027, although it no longer anticipates a move to $1.20. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)
